newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast Lt. crudes jump with NYMEX Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast Lt. crudes jump with NYMEX Friday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot crude markets turned quiet Friday, as sharply higher prices prompted crude oil buyers to start to the weekend early, traders said.
In futures markets, June deliveries of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 82 cents a barrel to $22.12, sparking a similar rally in WTI spot markets.
Futures prices gained momentum after June contracts broke through key price levels Friday, signaling a stronger market for analysts who chart crude oil values.

The benchmark West Coast grade, Alaska North Slope (ANS), tracked the rise in futures and spot marekts, but forced refiners to the sidelines amid fears higher costs of raw material would cut into their profits, traders said.

"You saw crude take a $1.50 jump last week. Products are doing a whole lot to follow," one trader said, noting today's rises would further cap profits, and leave open the possibility of production cutbacks.
Outright ANS prices rose 80 cents a barrel to $20.50/20.70 a barrel.
Meanwhile, ANS discounts crude have remained stagnant since last week's sale of two cargoes at lower discounts.
ANS last sold at a $1.50 discount ot West Texas Intermediate.
BP, the biggest producer of ANS, continued to offer ANS at $1.30 under WTI, its price since Monday.
Kern River crude prices remained flat after Monday's rise in postings, to $14.50/14.60 a barrel.
Line 63 markets remained idle, while asphalt crude Wilmington rose with postings to $16.35/16.45.
